newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Veteran Australian judge dies, aged 94.
newsitem.headline: Veteran Australian judge dies, aged 94.

text.p: Sir Garfield Barwick, who spent 17 years as Australia's most senior judge and gave the constitutional advice that led to the historic 1975 sacking of Gough Whitlam's Labor government, has died at the age of 94.
Barwick died on Sunday in a Sydney nursing home, it was reported on Tuesday.
Barwick, a small, combative man, rose from a working-class Sydney background to become a successful city barrister and powerful courtroom advocate.
Within months of starting a political career at age 55 he was attorney-general in the Liberal government of Sir Robert Menzies, whom he later served as foreign minister from 1961-64.
After a rival was favoured to succeed Menzies as Liberal Party head, Barwick returned to the law and from 1964 he became Chief Justice of the High Court, a post he held until 1981.
His influence in that job was far-reaching -- he is remembered among other things for a literal interpretation of Australian tax laws which critics said encouraged tax avoidance.

But his closest brush with history came in November 1975 when he advised then governor general Sir John Kerr that it was within his power to sack Labor prime minister Gough Whitlam when the country's financial stability was threatened.
The move, which was formally sanctioned by Britain's Queen Elizabeth as Australia's head of state, caused the worst constitutional crisis in modern Australian history.
Barwick said later that he had not been politically inspired but opponents, mostly from Whitlam's Labor party, said the judge had over-stepped the boundaries of his role.
